assumptions.original: On a positive finite time horizon, the given filtration and finite sample measure satisfy the usual conditions used to construct the completed Itô integral. The integrand is real and progressive with finite product-space squared energy, and the scalar Brownian driver is relative to the given filtration. The grid satisfies 0 ≤ t₀ ≤ ⋯ ≤ tₙ ≤ T. A grid with no cells and repeated endpoints are allowed.
assumptions.reconstructed: eta is strongly progressive for F and (omega,r)↦eta(r,omega) is in L²(mu⊗lambda_T). B satisfies standard scalar Brownian finite-dimensional distributions: for every finite nonnegative time set S, (B_s)_{s∈S} has centered Gaussian law with covariance (s,t)↦min(s,t), and B has continuous paths mu-a.e. In particular B_0=0 is required almost surely, not for every sample, is strongly adapted to F, and B_t-B_s is independent of F_s for every s≤t. F is right-continuous and every subset S⊆Omega with mu(S)=0 belongs to F_t for every t≥0. The time list is nondecreasing, not necessarily strictly increasing; its final value is at most T.
assumptions.evidence: Full-module binder and definition audit: The grid signature requires Monotone times and only the last bound, not times_0=0 or times_n=T. The private concatenation helper proves the Ico cell union; the public proof uses actual-process increment isometry.

conclusion.original: Take a scalar completed Itô integral of a progressive square-integrable integrand. The sum of its squared increments along a finite nondecreasing deterministic grid is integrable. Its expectation is the integrand's squared energy over the half-open span of the grid. Formula: \mathbb E\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(I_{t_{i+1}}-I_{t_i})^2=\int_{\Omega\times[t_0,t_n)}|\eta_r(\omega)|^2\,d(\mu\otimes dt).
conclusion.reconstructed: I is the specified continuous completed Ito integral of eta against B: the canonical elementary-integral limit off its null uniform-Cauchy exceptional set, zero on that set, and constant after T. Let S(omega)=∑_{r=0}^{n-1}(I(times_{r+1},omega)-I(times_r,omega))². Then S is mu-integrable and ∫S dmu=∫_{Omega×[times_0,times_n)} eta(v,omega)² d(mu⊗lambda_T)(omega,v).
